text:
Quinton Byfield has had a busy two weeks. He won a game in overtime after the Kings nearly blew a four-goal lead (The Hockey News), scored twice on the power play this week (RotoWire), and found his name in a trade scenario linking him to Elias Pettersson (The Times of India). Rumors aside, the Kings are leaning on him more: he's on the ice for 77% of their power-play time after 44% last season.

His own chances are up, to 1.21 expected goals per 60 from 0.82, and at 5v5 the Kings are about nine points better in expected-goal share (the quality of chances) with him on. So why only six points in 12 games? Los Angeles has scored 8.0 fewer goals than its chances with him out there, one of the worst luck gaps in the league, and that usually swings back. Evolving-Hockey had him 90th percentile among forwards at driving play last season. Twelve games is a small sample, but the second pick of 2020 looks closer to a breakout than his points suggest. Our projection has 36 to 58 more points.
headline: Byfield is better than his six points
